mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions that support corporate revenue growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of months with positive PAYEMS month-over-month change, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that dampens economic activity and corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous month-over-month increase in consumer spending (RSAFS) and decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) signals robust economic momentum, but when industrial production (INDPRO) is below 110, the momentum is perceived as fragile due to manufacturing weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where RSAFS and UNRATE are both moving in the expected direction and INDPRO < 110, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising for 3 consecutive months), a declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates an overheating labor market that fuels inflation, prompting further rate hikes and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS has risen for 3 consecutive months and UNRATE is declining, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals robust consumer demand for housing and related sectors, which typically translates to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of months with positive HOUST month-over-month change, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 110 indicates a contraction in manufacturing output, which typically precedes a slowdown in corporate earnings and causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO < 110, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in CPI (CPIAUCSL) and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals aggressive monetary policy to combat inflation, but when unemployment (UNRATE) is rising, it indicates economic weakness that amplifies stagflation concerns, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS are both rising and UNRATE > 4.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in consumer spending (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average indicates a weakening in the primary driver of economic growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS < 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.
